text.p: - Four ministerial candidates proposed by prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek last Friday were approved by parliamentary board on Wednesday after a hearing.
- Drnovsek on Wednesday proposed Ales Zalar as his candidate for minister of justice and Joze Protner for minister of agriculture.

- The growing number of Slovenian companies borrowing money from abroad show that confidence in local banks is low and that foreign competition among Slovenian banks is necessary, Slovenia's Chamber of Economy said.
- Slovenian foreign exchange reserves in November fell by $24 million to $4.268 billion, the Bank of Slovenia said.
- The national radio and television on Wednesday signed an deal with Italian and Hungarian minorities to transmit programmes for minorities.
- Slovenia beat Finland 90-77 on Wednesday in a qualifying game for the European basketball championship.

- More than 49 percent of people disagreed with the decision of the conservative People's Party not to join a government coalition of four parties, 31 percent supported the party's decision, while almost 19 percent were undecided about the issue, an opinion poll by the paper showed.

- The centre-left Liberal Democrats, the biggest party in the government coalition, will continue its efforts to enlarge the coalition in order to gain broader support for key projects, the party's general secretary Gregor Golobic said.
